source.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Zhengxuan Wu; Aryaman Arora; Atticus Geiger; Zheng Wang; Jing Huang; Daniel Jurafsky; Christopher D. Manning; Christopher Potts

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened in the extraction; the SAE AUROC values below come from the more clearly laid-out Table 4a.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates pretrained SAE features on Gemma models for concept detection, extending SAE-feature evaluation to this LLM benchmark. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates SAE feature activations for concept detection and SAE-based steering. Only the concept-detection results are rows for V4; steering scores do not directly measure whether an SAE recovers a feature. The paper also reports cited prior work, which is not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well GemmaScope SAE latents detect labelled concepts in Gemma-2-2B/9B residual streams (AUROC, F1). This bears directly on V4's claim that a dictionary can recover sparse features in LLMs. It does not touch toy-model geometry, capacity, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that prompting outperforms all representation steering methods, followed by finetuning. For concept detection, simple supervised representation methods (DiffMean, Probe, ReFT-r1) perform best, and SAEs are not competitive on either axis. They introduce ReFT-r1 as competitive on both tasks. They suggest SAE underperformance partly reflects shallow auto-interp labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates pretrained GemmaScope SAE features on an LLM benchmark; it does not reproduce toy-network training or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model layer; for example, the reported SAE AUROC differs across the four tested layers.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE decoder directions used for steering score far below prompting, finetuning and DiffMean (overall score avg 0.165 vs DiffMean 0.239, Prompt 0.894). Clamping is worse than addition, and SAE-A steers no better than SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features recovered from LLMs are less causally effective steering handles than simple supervised directions.

record.problems: The benchmark uses synthetic, LLM-generated data and SAE concept lists derived from an automated interpretability pipeline; the authors say those labels may be shallow. For Gemma-2-2B, the available SAE is for the base LM, while the model evaluation is instruction-tuned. These results do not measure superposition geometry or establish completeness and stability of SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V4 concept-detection rows were retained from the flattened main Table 1 because its individual values could not be assigned confidently to model-layer columns. Table 4a supplies the layer-specific SAE values recorded above. SAE steering results were excluded because they do not directly measure V4.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity-dependent phase transition, no feature geometry.
All: no test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
All: no analysis of polysemantic neurons or their origins.
Whether features are spread across many neurons; SAE recovery beyond two Gemma models, four residual-stream sites and auto-interp-labelled concepts.
Completeness, stability across seeds/sizes, and canonicity of SAE features are not measured.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: SAE-A (AUROC-selected SAE latent) concept-detection AUROC per site: 0.924, 0.924, 0.911, 0.907 (avg 0.917)
F1 for SAE vs other methods under balanced and ~1% positive imbalanced settings; text says SAEs perform poorly despite their sparsity
SAE average AUROC across sites, 0.695, currently mislabeled as 9B L20

record.verdict_notes: The reader misread Table 4a's column order, so r3 records the SAE average instead of 9B L20. The key V4 evidence of SAE-A was omitted. For Gemma-2-2B, the SAEs were trained on the base model but applied to the instruction-tuned model. Concept data are synthetic, generated by gpt-4o-mini.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and feature geometry.
Whether capacity competition explains polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-based concept detection for selected GemmaScope concepts, not whether LLM features are generally spread across many neurons or whether SAE recovery generalizes across models and concepts.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical representation units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features as units of superposition.

relationships.condition: Vanilla GemmaScope SAE latents matched to concepts by their auto-interp label (Gemma-2-2B L10/L20, Gemma-2-9B L20/L31, CONCEPT500)
relationships.reason: AUROCs of 0.631–0.755 are above chance but significantly below five supervised methods (DiffMean 0.92–0.96). SAEs also perform poorly on F1 under 1% class imbalance. Recovery of labelled concepts is incomplete (r1–r4; F1 from Figure 3, not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: AUROCs of 0.631–0.755 were above chance but significantly below five supervised methods (DiffMean 0.92–0.96), and SAEs did poorly on F1 under 1% class imbalance, so recovery of labelled concepts was incomplete.
